source_title: Clean permit
semantic_reason: The rule is unchanged: one permission matches, no constraint binds. The only difference is expression, not outcome: the budget hold is now a typed quota_reservation obligation attached by a requirement policy rather than an implicit side effect of a ceiling.

source_title: Permissive posture, zero grants
semantic_reason: ADR-065 owns default deny as a product and security decision and removes the per-tool unmatched=Permit posture. A read-only label is not sufficient reason to fail open, because a read can disclose sensitive data, enumerate authorization structure, or feed a later write. NotApplicable maps to deny in the production profile; the permissive arm survives only as an explicit, action-scoped, time-bound compatibility exception.

source_title: Grants union across groups
semantic_reason: The union-of-permissions point is unchanged and is the reason the case exists. The verdict is not: approval is a stateful requirement rather than a value in the verdict lattice, so the result is a permit carrying an outstanding approval requirement and the operational state is CHALLENGE.

source_title: A restriction group changes the outcome
semantic_reason: The mechanism is unchanged: a group carrying a restriction narrows a request that an identical principal without that group is allowed outright. The verdict form changes for the same reason as EX-03.

source_title: A satisfied exception collapses a ceiling
semantic_reason: The exception mechanism is unchanged and still collapses the policy to non-applicable through the same code path as the policy not existing. The verdict form changes for the same reason as EX-03.

source_title: Two independent reasons to deny
semantic_reason: An explicit constraint denies and the trace reports the absent permission as well, so a requester is not sent to fix half the problem. Both halves are asserted.

source_title: Conjunctive ceiling exceeds the meet of its parts
semantic_reason: The arithmetic claim does not survive, because ADR-065 never collapses approval clauses, so there is no meet whose quorum could be bounded by its parts. The claim that survives is the one that mattered: a conjunctive tag selector is load bearing, because it is the only way to make a requirement apply to a PAIR of tags rather than to either tag alone.

source_title: Pool intersection and quorum max
semantic_reason: ADR-065 rejects the source meet outright. The conjunction of two threshold clauses is satisfiable by approvers the intersection excludes, so reducing two clauses to one over the intersected pool with the maximum quorum produces denials the policy set does not require. Clauses are retained as a conjunction and deduplicate without flattening pools.

source_title: Disjoint pools are unsatisfiable
semantic_reason: The denial was an artifact of the collapsing algebra rather than of the policy set: two clauses over disjoint pools are each independently satisfiable. With the collapse removed the request challenges. Whether an eligible pool can actually produce its quorum is a directory fact resolved at discharge time, which ADR-065 does not specify as a decision-time rule; that gap is raised on the ADR pull request rather than resolved here by inventing semantics.

source_title: Pool too small for the quorum
semantic_reason: Same correction as EX-09. Neither the quorum nor the pool of a clause is adjusted by the presence of another clause, which is asserted directly: the quorum-two clause keeps its quorum and its single declared group.

source_title: Self-exclusion flips a satisfiable escalation
semantic_reason: Self-approval exclusion is retained as separation_of_duties carried on the composed requirement, not as a decision-time reduction of the eligible pool. Shrinking the pool at decision time would bake a membership snapshot into the challenge, and eligibility has to be rechecked at approval and again immediately before execution in any case.

source_title: Inherited ceiling with a witness path
semantic_reason: The witness requirement is unchanged and is asserted through the audience-scoped trace: the operator projection names the inherited group and its source class. The verdict form changes for the same reason as EX-03.

source_title: Cyclic group graph terminates correctly
semantic_reason: Unchanged. The transitive closure of a cyclic digraph is the reachable set, so a cycle is a correctness non-issue and an operational signal. The case asserts the decision is identical with and without the cycle.

source_title: Truncated closure, posture decides
semantic_reason: Both arms are non-permits under ADR-065. The permissive arm is removed with the per-tool on_error posture. The read-only arm still resolves rather than erroring, but through the Kleene short-circuit rather than through a posture: the action selector is determinately false, so no group-scoped policy could have applied and the unknown closure cannot matter. Group closure enters the evaluator as an ordinary tri-state attribute, so truncation needs no special code path.

source_title: Policy information point down in a grant
semantic_reason: The source SKIPPED an unevaluable permission and denied, because routing it through a per-tool on_error posture whose value could be Permit would let an outage increase access. ADR-065 removes that posture, so the honest result is available without risk: an unknown permission is reported as indeterminate and still cannot grant.

source_title: Kleene short-circuit removes spurious indeterminacy
semantic_reason: Unchanged. A condition with a known-false conjunct is determinately false even when another term is unavailable, so the permission is a clean non-match and no unknown is recorded. Asserted against EX-15, which is the identical outage with a different amount.

source_title: Policy information point down in a ceiling
semantic_reason: The rule is unchanged: an unknown constraint cannot be skipped, because a constraint bounds every permission and treating it as inapplicable raises the roof. What changes is where the result lands. The source routed indeterminacy through a per-tool on_error posture that could be Permit; ADR-065 maps it to the ERROR state, which never executes.

source_title: Indeterminacy resolves when it cannot matter
semantic_reason: ADR-065 does not reproduce the source lo/hi collapse. The combining rule tests constraint uncertainty BEFORE permission coverage, so an unknown constraint is indeterminate whether or not an unrelated permission happened to be absent. The cost is availability during a dependency outage; the gain is that each policy contribution stays locally checkable rather than depending on the state of every other policy.

source_title: Union across ceilings
semantic_reason: Unchanged. Obligations from several requirement policies union, and per-leaf resolution places each transform on the leaf its target covers.

source_title: Equal-rank obligation conflict
semantic_reason: The outcome for the enforcement point is the same in the source world, because the tool it used had on_error Deny. The authorization value differs and that difference is deliberate: a conflicting mandatory obligation is a defect in the policy set, not a dependency that failed, so it denies rather than becoming indeterminate. Silently picking one transform is refused in both models.

source_title: Per-leaf rank-max in both directions
semantic_reason: The per-leaf resolution is unchanged and is still correct in both directions. The ORDER is inverted and re-founded: ADR-065 ranks by information disclosed and selects the least disclosing comparable transform, where the source ranked by destructiveness and selected the maximum. The two agree everywhere except tokenization, which leaves the chain entirely because a value recoverable from a vault does not reveal less than a one-way digest.

source_title: An unsupported obligation denies
semantic_reason: Unchanged, and extended: a PEP that advertised no profile at all is also refused rather than being treated as needing nothing.

source_title: Reserve then commit
semantic_reason: The lifecycle is unchanged. The expression changes: a budget is a typed quota_reservation obligation attached by a requirement policy and discharged by a coordinator outside the pure evaluator, rather than a field on a ceiling evaluated inside condition evaluation. The idempotency key is the decision binding rather than an argument hash, which the source prohibited but did not have a binding wide enough to supply.

source_title: A failed execution releases its hold
semantic_reason: Unchanged. The decision was correct and stays correct; only the reservation unwinds, and a released hold cannot then be committed.

source_title: Concurrent escalations hold the budget
semantic_reason: The property is unchanged and is the reason reservation happens at decision time rather than at approval time. The verdict form changes for the same reason as EX-03, and the late conversion from permit to deny is reported in the trace as a reservation failure rather than as a policy denial that never happened.

source_title: Approval timeout releases and applies on_timeout
semantic_reason: The operational outcome is the same and the RULE that reaches it is not, which is what this disposition records. ADR-065 prohibits on_timeout=permit outright, so the source's configurable timeout posture is gone: a non-response never proves approval, and permitting after a timeout would additionally admit execution against a hold that has already been released. The case runs the timeout, asserts the denial and its reason, and asserts the counter is back to zero.

source_title: An agent more privileged than its principal
semantic_reason: Unchanged and structural. Each hop of the actor chain carries its own identity attributes and is evaluated in its own realm, and the chain meets. Union across the chain is the confused deputy.

source_title: Delegation depth exceeded
semantic_reason: Unchanged. Depth is a topology constraint checked at admission, before any policy is loaded, which the case asserts by requiring an empty determining set.

source_title: Signals accumulate past a threshold
semantic_reason: Weighted accumulation is retained. Its placement changes: the accumulated score arrives as the tri-state attribute signal.risk_score produced by the inspection plane, and the policies that ACT on it are ordinary constraint and requirement policies. That is how ADR-065 expresses assurance classes, and it is what makes a detection plane that cannot answer fail closed instead of quietly scoring zero.

source_title: Detection cannot raise a decision
semantic_reason: Unchanged and made structural: the authoring validator refuses an inspection policy that declares itself mandatory, so a heuristic cannot become a required control without being registered as one.

source_title: An unevaluable detector does not fail the request
semantic_reason: Unchanged, including the second half that is easy to lose: a detector that DID match contributes its obligations on evidence rather than on outcome, so the elevated audit record is written even though the score changed nothing. The deliberate asymmetry with a gating control is asserted separately.

source_title: Approval rebinding after an argument change
semantic_reason: Unchanged in effect and wider in scope. ADR-065 rejects the source binding as too narrow and binds the complete normalized input, so the amount change is caught by the same digest that catches an identity, epoch, registry or attribute change.

source_title: Break-glass pierces a pierceable ceiling
semantic_reason: Unchanged, with one widening that the ADR-065 policy model forces: an approval ceiling is a requirement rather than a constraint, so piercing has to apply to requirements as well or an emergency override could not bypass the approval it exists to bypass. The mandatory audit and notification obligations are unconditional.

source_title: Break-glass cannot pierce a regulatory ceiling
semantic_reason: Unchanged. An empty pierceable list is the difference between a control and a suggestion.

source_title: Authority from untrusted input, rejected at save time
semantic_reason: Unchanged. The rule fires on identity comparisons between a caller-supplied term and a trusted one, and the bounding form of the same comparison stays legal, because bounding untrusted input is the entire point of an argument limit.

source_title: Unknown tool
semantic_reason: Unchanged. An unregistered surface is refused at admission with a reason distinguishable from a registered action that has no matching permission, because the two need different fixes.

source_title: A schema violation catches the unit bug
semantic_reason: Unchanged. The typed argument schema refuses both the unknown field and the missing required one, and the case asserts the explanation names both.

source_title: Named-level projection, no traversal
semantic_reason: Unchanged. The mapping names the leaf and the resolver supplies the ancestors, which the case asserts by checking the provenance class of the materialized level.

source_title: Ceiling scoped by a projected ancestor attribute
semantic_reason: The mechanism is unchanged and is the point of the case: the entire difference from EX-38 is an attribute of a resource the principal never named. The verdict form changes for the same reason as EX-03.

source_title: A recursive subtree ceiling outranks a segment exception
semantic_reason: Unchanged. An exception clause only ever relaxes the policy it lives on, so principal-side and resource-side scoping compose without either overriding the other.

source_title: A sibling subtree is unaffected
semantic_reason: The mechanism is unchanged and the case is paired with EX-40 as a regression test for scope leakage in either direction. The verdict form changes for the same reason as EX-03. The obligation set differs from EX-40's sibling because disclosure transforms expand over the ACTION's declared response leaves, and the two actions declare different ones.

source_title: Multi-parent resource, reachability by any path
semantic_reason: Unchanged. A resource reachable from a restricted container is restricted even though it is also filed somewhere benign; intersecting the scopes along each path would let anything escape any constraint by also being linked into an open one.

source_title: A truncated resource closure fails closed
semantic_reason: The rule is unchanged and the landing place moves for the same reason as EX-17. A partial closure may be missing the very ancestor a constraint is scoped to, so it is never evaluated against.

source_title: Parentage changes between decision and execution
semantic_reason: The operational outcome is the same and the RULE that reaches it is not, which is what this disposition records. The source needed a SECOND context hash because its request hash covered only what the caller supplied and the ancestors were materialized afterwards. ADR-065 binds the complete normalized input including every resolver-materialized attribute, so one binding covers both and there is no second digest for a caller to forget to carry. The case rebinds a decision made before the move against the request presented after it and asserts the refusal.

source_title: An empty closure is authoritative, not an error
semantic_reason: The source case is internally inconsistent and this row records its DECLARED result rather than its worked trace: the case badge says Permit while its own trace concludes Escalate, because the fixture's organization-scoped spend requirement applies to the amount used. ADR-065 reaches CHALLENGE under either reading, so the change is recorded against the declared result, which is the larger of the two. The distinction the case exists for is unchanged and is asserted directly: the closure is KNOWN and empty rather than unknown, organization-scoped policies still bind, and the principal-scoped permission is what carries a subject whose realm has no group concept.

source_title: An approver pool in a non-interactive realm
semantic_reason: Unchanged, and relocated to the ADR-065 policy lifecycle validation step, which validates authority, obligations and capabilities before a bundle can be compiled. Enforcing it on the realm keeps the evaluator out of the business of deciding which subjects are people.

source_title: A validly signed token from an undeclared realm
semantic_reason: Unchanged. Unknown surface and unknown issuer are both refused before any policy loads. Omitting this check lets a principal reach evaluation with an undefined realm, where a falsy default reads as an absent group graph, makes an empty closure look authoritative, and silently skips every group-scoped constraint: a fail-open produced entirely by omission.
